items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: But that's how I learned how to play a show; Tom Whaley taught me.

ctx.x: they ran over it again, I would start playing. And I'd be playing it -- and I'd be playing it right; I didn't know what I was doing, but whatever I did, it was right; it was acceptable.

Now, we're getting ready to play the first show, this Friday morning -- I'm scared to death. So I went to Tom and I said, "Mr. Whaley, I've never played a show before in my life, and I don't know how to play this show; I don't know what to do." And he turned to me and said, "You mean to tell me you were downstairs yesterday and you were playing and you don't ..." And I said, "I can't read anything." And he said, "Oh my God. Well, I tell you what you do. Keep your foot off that bass drum, don't play that bass drum…

And I never forgot that; that's the reason I could play a show and didn't even have to have any music if I have somebody up front that could give me the right downbeat and everything; I have no problems at all, playing the show. But that's how I learned how to play a show; Tom Whaley taught me.
